service.description: Whether the Login screen offers its Test Login button, the john.doe login with the password moqui (SEC-RTE-17): only on a dev or test instance (instance@purpose), or where demo@test-login is true (the demo component's conf sets it for a public demo), and only while EX_JOHN_DOE's password is still moqui. That check is a slow hash an anonymous render would run each time, so its answer is kept a minute in the local cache webroot.login.test, keyed by a digest of the stored hash: a new password is a new key.

Whether the system has no user accounts yet, so the first administrator is to be created: the Login screen's create form, its initialAdminNeeded transition and the terminal's login dialog ask this, and create#InitialAdminAccount refuses unless it holds. Seed data has accounts nobody logs in as, which do not count: _NA_, the edge node's delegate _EDGE_ (EdgeSetupData.xml) and the chat users of agents (AgentTypeData.xml). It is needed only while user-facade/login@initial-admin-enabled is true (MoquiDefaultConf.xml, false by default): with no account and the property off, needed is false and disabled is true. The password rules are answered only while needed is true.

parameter.description: No account exists, but user-facade/login@initial-admin-enabled is not true, so the first administrator cannot be created now.

parameter.description: The one-time setup secret the server writes to its startup log while no account exists; not needed for a request from this machine (ec.user.initialAdminLocal).

parameter.name: joinAdvanced
parameter.description: Also put the account in ADMIN_ADV (Administrators - Advanced: login as another user, the SQL runner, the SSH admin shell, conf edit, component deploy and the other sealed tools). ADMIN_ADV is a privileged group, so only a member can add a member later; this is the way in for the first one.

service.description: Who may act on an account's sign-in (its factors and codes, its sign-in fields): its own user, for an action that makes or ends a factor or codes (recentAuth) only after signing in, or confirming who they are, in the last five minutes (org.moqui.sso.RecentAuthServices.require#RecentAuth; SEC-ADM-03); another user only with permissionId (NONE: any caller the service's authorization lets in) and, for a change (bounded), when the account holds no access the caller lacks (Identity.js heldBeyond: a privileged group the caller is not in, a sealed permission the caller does not hold; SEC-ADM-04, SEC-ADM-05), and for a recentAuth action after the caller's own sign-in in the last five minutes, as for their own account. With nobody signed in (the sign-in services, which act for a pre-authenticated user before the login and check that user themselves) and for a caller that disabled authorization (a job, a setup service) the caller answers for it. A refusal is an error and allowed false. anonymous-all because those sign-in services call it with nobody signed in; it grants nothing.

The take is one conditional update committed at once (ec.user.takeFactorCode), and the code verifies only when this call took it: of two right submissions of one code only one verifies, and a code taken stays used up even when the caller's transaction then rolls back, as update#Password does when it refuses the new password (a new code is then needed; SEC-WEB-87).

The current user's SSH keys, newest first, for an account page: never another user's, whatever is passed. Ended keys (delete#UserSshKey) only with includeEnded. The public key itself is not given, only its type and fingerprint; when a key was last used is not kept. An error with no user logged in.

parameter.description: Maps: sshKeyId (for delete#UserSshKey), description, keyType (ssh-ed25519), fingerprint (SHA256:..., as ssh-keygen -l prints), fromDate (when it was added), thruDate

It is shown only in the out parameters; only its hash is stored, as a UserLoginKey. Needs a sign-in in the last five minutes (require#RecentAuth).

service.description: End one of the current user's access tokens, by its tokenId (as find#UserAccessTokens and create#UserAccessToken give it) or its loginKey (the stored hash); either parameter takes either value. Another user's token, and one that is not there, is "no such access token".

A new key of the current user that opens one service alone (UserLoginKey.scope): gateway, the LLM gateway's /llm/v1, which the web, REST, git and every other login refuse. It is in the user's device list under deviceName (revoke#UserDeviceKey ends it) and good for login-key/@device-expire-hours. Shown only in the out parameters. A dev instance keeps one for its group server's gateway (plans/design-dev-aide.md 21.2), in place of the account's key.

parameter.name: scope
parameter.description: gateway

parameter.name: deviceName

service.description: End a key of the current user by the key itself, as its holder keeps it: a client let go ends the keys it held (a scoped key, and the key it signs in with). A key that is not the user's is not ended (revoked false).

A new app password for the current user, for one device or app and one protocol (scope): only that protocol's server takes it, with the username; the web login does not. It is shown only in the out parameters (20 letters and digits in groups of four); only its hash is stored. Needs a sign-in in the last five minutes (require#RecentAuth).

parameter.name: name
parameter.description: The device or app, such as "Pat's iPhone"

parameter.name: scope
parameter.description: dav (CalDAV, CardDAV, WebDAV), ssh (SSH, SFTP, git over SSH), git (git over HTTP), xmpp, or ai (the LLM gateway, A2A, MCP)

service.description: Revoke one of the current user's app passwords: the device using it is refused from now on.
The current user's app passwords, newest first: appPasswordId, name, scope, createdDate, lastUsedDate, and revokedDate (revoked ones only with includeRevoked). No password or hash.

The current user's devices signed in by key: the desktop and mobile clients, each a UserLoginKey made by the REST login with createLoginKey and deviceName (plans/Mobile-Desktop.md, MD3). Unexpired ones, most recently used first: loginKey (the stored hash, which names the device for revoke), deviceName, fromDate, lastUsedDate, thruDate, and current (the device of this request's login_key header).
Sign one of the current user's devices out, by its loginKey (the stored hash): its next request is refused, and its notification socket closes within a minute.

A new key for the device of this request's login_key header, with the same deviceName and a full login-key/@device-expire-hours, given once; the header's key ends ten minutes later, so requests already sent with it still pass. An error when the request was not signed in by a device key of the user's.
